official.title: Innovation Postdoc – Artificial Intelligence
official.description_text:
Aalto University is home to researchers working at the frontier of artificial intelligence. Some of that work has the potential to become more than research — to address real problems, create new industries, and contribute to Finland's deep tech future. The Innovation Postdoc exists to support that transition.
This is a 12-month funded position for doctoral researchers and postdocs who have a concrete result, technology, or invention with commercial potential, and who are ready to dedicate their full focus to exploring it. You will work on validating your technology with real users and partners, developing a business model, and preparing for the next step — whether that is external investment, a spinout, or another commercialisation pathway — supported by Aalto's innovation infrastructure, coaching network, and peer community.
No prior business experience is required. What we are looking for is research with genuine differentiation, and a researcher with the drive to find out what it can become.
What you will do
As an ‘Innovation Postdoc’, your work is 100% focused on increasing the
innovation readiness level
of your research. Your responsibilities include:
Conducting structured problem and market validation through customer discovery interviews and stakeholder engagement
Developing technology if needed – with ‘product’ in mind.
Testing and iterating your technology with real-world users and partners
Developing a compelling business model and go-to-market strategy
Preparing for external investment, spinout formation, or other commercialization pathways
Participating in the Innovation Postdoc program activities, coaching sessions, and peer community (eg trade fair, Business Generator workshops, some events at The Founder House Helsinki etc.)
Who we are looking for
You do not need a business background, but you must be ready to adapt. We are looking for researchers with the mindset of a founder.
Required:
Doctoral degree (PhD) completed or submitted the thesis, from Aalto University
You have a doctoral degree in other universities, but working at Aalto University as a postdoctoral researcher
A concrete research result, technology, or invention with a clear differentiation and commercial potential in the corresponding field
Demonstrated ability to work independently and drive projects forward under uncertainty
We value attitudes like:
Obsession with a real-world problem, not just the technology – you are driven by the desire to solve something that matters
Coachability and open-mindedness – you are ready to step outside the academic bubble, actively seek feedback from customers and mentors, and change course when the evidence demands it
Adaptability and resilience – you understand that building a deep-tech spinout is a journey of uncertainty, and you treat setbacks as data, not failure
Business curiosity – you do not need a degree, but you are genuinely interested in how value is created and captured. You think about markets, customers, and competition, not just technical performance.
Eagerness for impact – you have a technology with strong differentiation and are motivated to see it applied and scaled in the real world.
‘can-do’ attitude – you are ready to figure out what you don't know, roll up your sleeves, and get things done even without a clear roadmap
What we offer
We provide an environment for innovation, removing the friction so you can focus on building.
Funded Runway
: A 12-month salaried contract at the postdoctoral researcher level, focused 100% on increasing the innovation readiness of your work
Milestone-based funding top-ups
to support validation activities, prototyping, or external engagement
Structured milestone framework
: clear deliverables and check-ins throughout the program to keep your validation on track
Scientific mentorship
: continued access to and support from Aalto professors and domain experts to ensure your technology development stays rigorous
Access to Aalto's research infrastructures
– depending on the field, such as BioEconomy facilities, computing clusters, LUMI Supercomputer, OtaNano, and more.
Dedicated Innovation Space
: A physical environment designed for commercialization, separated from daily academic duties, based in A-Grid
Streamlined IP Suppor
t: Professional guidance on IP transfer and standardized spinout terms designed to attract top-tier investors
Aalto Inventors community
– peer cohort of fellow deep-tech researchers across fields, building alongside you
Access to Aalto Inventors and Business Generator accelerator workshops
: hands-on sessions covering the full journey from lab to market
Extensive Network
: Personalized coaching from a curated network of deep-tech investors, serial entrepreneurs and industry leaders – including founding partners of top Nordic VC funds and executives with successful exits.
Access to The Founders House Helsinki
- events, community, and co-working space at the heart of Helsinki's startup scene
Pathway into the Nordic startup ecosystem
– including access to the Slush Spinout track
Comprehensive toolkit
to build up your business knowledge
The position includes occupational health care and retirement benefits in accordance with Finnish employment law and the collective agreement for Finnish universities.
Application instructions
Before applying, please read this instruction carefully. The applications must be submitted through Aalto University’s recruitment system.
The steps required for submission are outlined here.
The application portal closes on August 23th, 2026, 23:59. We recommend you submit your application a couple of days prior to the deadline to ensure proper processing.
Documents and naming conventions
The documents mentioned below must be submitted as part of the Innovation Postdoc application. All documents must be submitted as PDF files (max. 5 MB in total) unless otherwise stated. Please use the following naming conventions for your documents and add your full name on each page of documents.
FamilyName_Firstname-degree transcript
FamilyName_First name-Innovation Statement: Tell us why you are obsessed with this problem/opportunity, a time you failed and recovered, and what non-technical skills you want to master (1 page)
FamilyName_Firstname-Path to Pilot: Your roadmap for problem validation (1 page)
FamilyName_Firstname-CV
Any other materials you want to present, Familyname_Firstname-FILENAME
Video presentation upload
Please upload your video presentation as MP4 to a plafrom of your choice. The video should not exceed 90 seconds. Generate a link to the video and paste it into the respective field in the application form.
Please submit all materials in English.
For further information and questions, contact Myungji Suh
myungji.suh@aalto.fi
.

ai.summary: Aalto's Innovation Postdoc program targets researchers with a concrete, commercially differentiable technology or invention ready for validation with real users and partners. The 12-month position focuses 100% on de-risking innovation (problem/market validation, business model development, commercialization pathway preparation) rather than research advancement, supported by coaching, IP guidance, and access to the Nordic startup ecosystem.

thematic_fit.rationale: The position is explicitly innovation/commercialization-focused, not research-focused. The researcher's target identity is 'design and evaluate human-centred immersive systems' — grounded in rigorous HCI research methodology and spatial learning outcomes. A campus orientation XR application may have some real-world impact, but the posting makes clear this role is about business model development, market validation, customer discovery, and spinout readiness, not advancing spatial cognition or immersive learning science. The core mission divergence is fundamental.

methodological_fit.rationale: The researcher has strong user-studies and experimental-design skills (intermediate level), which intersect with the program's emphasis on 'testing and iterating with real-world users.' However, the posting does not describe research methodology as a core activity. It emphasizes customer discovery interviews, stakeholder engagement, and market/business model work — adjacent to but distinct from the researcher's HCI evaluation and validation expertise. The methodological overlap is shallow.

growth_value.rationale: This position would expose the researcher to commercialization, business strategy, investor relations, and go-to-market thinking — capabilities orthogonal to their target identity as an HCI researcher. While potentially valuable for personal development, the program is explicitly designed to pivot researchers toward entrepreneurship, not to deepen research capability in spatial cognition, collaborative immersive systems, or immersive learning. The program would close gaps in business knowledge, not research gaps.

strategic_value.rationale: Aalto University is a tier-1 institution with strong HCI and XR research groups (positive for future networking). The program offers excellent access to venture capital, serial entrepreneurs, and the Nordic startup ecosystem. However, the researcher's stated target positions are 'doctoral-researcher, PhD-candidate, project-researcher, research-assistant-with-phd-pathway' — none of which is a postdoc commercialization role. This position would delay doctoral study and redirect the researcher away from their stated PhD pathway. Strategic value is diminished by misalignment with career trajectory.

eligibility_flags: Requires completed PhD or submitted thesis by application/start date. Researcher currently holds MSc by Research in progress (thesis stage). Eligibility unclear unless thesis is submitted and accepted before program start.
Program is framed as 'postdoc' position for those with 'doctoral degree completed or submitted thesis.' Researcher has not completed doctorate and does not yet hold PhD.

Position explicitly requires 'a concrete research result, technology, or invention with clear differentiation and commercial potential.' The campus orientation XR system may qualify, but posting does not clarify whether an early-stage Master's project meets this bar or whether it must be a mature PhD-stage innovation.
risks: Career trajectory risk: Researcher's target identity emphasizes doctoral research and long-term HCI academia. A commercialization-focused postdoc would delay PhD entry and signal a pivot toward entrepreneurship rather than research.

Misaligned incentives: The program is structured to maximize innovation readiness and spinout potential, not research rigor. A researcher driven by 'design and evaluate' human-centred systems may experience friction with market-validation and business-model-first thinking.

Limited research continuation: Position offers 'continued access to and support from Aalto professors' for technology development, but does not position the researcher within an HCI or spatial cognition research group. Research mentorship appears secondary to innovation coaching.

Unclear scope: Posting does not specify whether XR/immersive learning systems are a priority research area for the program's innovation network. AI is mentioned as Aalto's frontier; XR application innovation fit is ambiguous.
Funding uncertainty: Milestone-based funding top-ups are mentioned but criteria and availability are not specified in the posting.
